message.reasoning: We need to answer based on policy excerpts. The question: "We think webhook payloads are being silently truncated for large records after a change on our own side — how do we build a batching strategy around the real limit?" They want to know how to build batching strategy around real limit. The policy says: Batching many changes into fewer webhook calls is not configurable — each change is delivered as its own event — so a batching strategy belongs on the receiving side, buffering fetched records rather than buffering webhook deliveries. Also, for large records, subscribe to .changed event and fetch current record by id, instead of relying on webhook payload. So answer: cannot batch on sending side; must buffer on receiving side. Use .changed event and fetch full record. Also note that payload is capped; truncated flag indicates need to fetch full record. So answer: explain that you can't configure batching; you need to handle on consumer side. Provide steps: subscribe to .changed, check truncated flag, fetch full record. Also mention that you can send test event. So answer accordingly.

function.arguments: {"message":"Hi! Webhook payloads are capped at a fixed size. If a record would exceed that size, the payload will contain only an id and a `truncated: true` flag – it’s not silently cut off. Because each change is sent as its own event, you can’t batch them on the sending side. Instead, build the batching logic on the receiving side: buffer the incoming events, and for any event that has `truncated: true` (or for records you know are large), use the record id to fetch the full record via the API. Subscribing to the `.changed` event and pulling the current record by id is the recommended way to avoid the size cap entirely. If you need a realistic sample to test against, you can use Settings → Developer → Webhooks → Send test event. Let me know if you’d like more details on setting that up!"}

arguments.message: Hi! Webhook payloads are capped at a fixed size. If a record would exceed that size, the payload will contain only an id and a `truncated: true` flag – it’s not silently cut off. Because each change is sent as its own event, you can’t batch them on the sending side. Instead, build the batching logic on the receiving side: buffer the incoming events, and for any event that has `truncated: true` (or for records you know are large), use the record id to fetch the full record via the API. Subscribing to the `.changed` event and pulling the current record by id is the recommended way to avoid the size cap entirely. If you need a realistic sample to test against, you can use Settings → Developer → Webhooks → Send test event. Let me know if you’d like more details on setting that up!
